# jeval

> jeval measures what a probabilistic classifier's confidence is actually worth on your own labeled
> decisions, and derives the confidence threshold at which a decision should be automated instead of
> handed to a human, from what a mistake costs. It reads JSONL decision records from disk. No
> server, no database, no network call, no account.

Machine-facing entry point. The human-facing version is [README.md](README.md); the task playbook
is [docs/agent-setup.md](docs/agent-setup.md).

## Install

Any of these works today. `pip install jeval` installs an unrelated project: that name on PyPI
belongs to someone else. Our distribution is `jeval-cli` and it is not published yet, so use one of
the commands above.

```sh
# no install, always current
uvx --from git+https://github.com/rlaope/jeval jeval --help

# pinned, no install
uvx --from git+https://github.com/rlaope/jeval@v0.1.2 jeval --help

# pinned wheel, installed
pip install https://github.com/rlaope/jeval/releases/download/v0.1.2/jeval_cli-0.1.2-py3-none-any.whl
```

## If you are an agent

The user's classifier returns a label and a confidence. Your job is to get measured numbers out of
their own data and show them the artifact — not to run a command tour.

1. See the shape of the output first, with no user data:
   `uvx --from git+https://github.com/rlaope/jeval jeval demo --out-dir /tmp/jeval-demo`
   It writes `report.html` (one self-contained file), `costs.yaml` and `.jeval/records.jsonl`.
2. Find the decision log: one row per model response, with the prediction, its confidence, and —
   for anything beyond a demo — the human's eventual answer. JSONL or CSV.
3. `jeval init --root DIR`, then describe that shape in `DIR/.jeval/ingest-map.yaml`.
   Keys: `field_map`, `questions_field`, `defaults`, `label_from`. A known vendor shape may already
   have a preset: `jeval ingest --list-presets`.
4. `jeval ingest <file> --root DIR`. It prints `wrote N records` and names every row it skipped and
   why. If N is 0, the mapping is wrong — fix the map, do not rewrite the user's data.
5. Labels are the gate. Without them jeval measures nothing and says
   `no labeled records`. Find them before promising a number (see the playbook).
6. `jeval report --root DIR --current <the threshold in production> --costs costs.yaml`
7. `jeval threshold --root DIR` writes `thresholds.yaml` — the artifact the application reads.
8. To keep it: `jeval drift --root DIR --fail-on ece-increase=0.05` exits 1 when the model degrades.

## Artifacts

| Path | What it is | Who reads it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `report.html` | One self-contained HTML file: verdict, reliability curve with intervals, cost curve, segments, drift | the human |
| `thresholds.yaml` | The threshold to deploy per action, with a bootstrap interval | the application |
| `labels.csv` | The decisions whose labels would teach the tool most | a person filling in answers |
| `calibration-*.yaml` | An optional correction map, exported only when the gain is real | the application |

## Hard facts, so you do not have to guess

- Records: `.jeval/records.jsonl`, one question per record, one JSON object per line.
- Question types: `choice`, `score`, `noul`. Accuracy is only defined for `choice`; `score`
  questions get MAE/RMSE/rank correlation and are never folded into binary accuracy.
- Cost matrix and threshold config live in files the user owns: `costs.yaml`, `thresholds.yaml`.
  jeval does not invent cost numbers. A threshold without costs is `not available`.
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` refused or nothing to measure (missing records, missing map, an
  input that cannot be true). Every refusal explains itself on stderr.
- The report never fetches anything at runtime and holds no token.
- `collect.track()` observes calls the application already makes; it never calls a model, never
  blocks, never raises. `JEVAL_COLLECT=0` disables it.
- No network access is needed by any command.

## Rules for an agent working with a user

- Never present a number the tool did not print. If the sample cannot support it, the tool says so
  and so must you.
- Never invent or edit the user's costs. Ask what a false positive and a false negative cost.
- Do not edit `.jeval/records.jsonl` by hand; ingest is the only writer.
- If there are no labels, say that plainly and offer the three label sources in the playbook
  instead of producing a report nobody can trust.
